reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous feature-level reasoning with external explainability tools to systematically identify distinguishing features between correct and incorrect predictions. Autonomous analysis allows for initial pattern detection based on known instance similarities and differences, while XAI tools provide quantitative, model-agnostic attributions to pinpoint which features drive the prediction divergence.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the feature values of individuals 21762 (correct) and 39470 (incorrect) to identify any striking differences in categorical or numerical features that may explain the misclassification.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that differ significantly between the correct and incorrect instances, highlighting potential drivers of misclassification

autonomous_tasks.query: Analyze the domain-level meaning of the differing features (e.g., age, workclass, education, marital status) and assess whether any of them are known to be strong predictors in the adult income classification task.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: High-level interpretation of why certain features may have stronger influence on the model's behavior in one instance versus another

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides interpretable, game-theoretic feature importance that captures how each feature contributes to the prediction difference between correct and incorrect cases. LIME offers local explanations to clarify how the model behaves around each instance. Integrated Gradients deliver smooth, continuous attributions to detect subtle shifts. Sensitivity analysis confirms which features are most sensitive to perturbation, validating their role in the misprediction.
